notes: Deck for TruthNet v0.3.3 (D-SITE-091, D-SITE-092, D-SITE-093). Acts: 1 = provenance warm-up (KS1), 2 = framing (KS2), 3 = feeling/system (KS3). All Act 2/3 cards carry a verify block (lateral-reading panel; 3 short lines, trimmed after Felix test). truth refers to what the card ASKS: provenance cards = the picture, veracity cards = the story/feeling. Outrage/scapegoat/urgency cards use fictional targets only — never a real school, place, group or person. Act 3 order puts the giveaway late so the sting (anchored to it) lands on its card. measure = the C1 learning instrument: matched novel pairs (one framing-fake + one plain-real each) answered cold before the deck and fresh after it, no reveals, no tokens; balanced real/fake so blanket scepticism scores 1/2, not 2/2.

cards.question: Real photo, or made by a computer?
cards.tellOk: Count the legs — there are more than four. And the grass melts into mush at the edges. No real dog looks like this; a computer drew it.
cards.tellNo: Count the legs — more than four. The grass melts into mush around the paws too. Classic signs a computer made the picture.

cards.cap: first proper run in the garden 🐾
cards.question: Real photo, or made by a computer?
cards.tellOk: Four legs, real fur, a real blurry background where the camera focused on the puppy. This one's a genuine photo.
cards.tellNo: This one's real — four legs, natural fur, and the soft out-of-focus background a real camera lens makes. Nothing a computer faked.

cards.cap: new sweet shop opened in town today 🍬
cards.question: Real photo, or made by a computer?
cards.tellOk: Read the sign — the letters are mushed-up nonsense. Computers are great at drawing sweets and terrible at spelling. A real shop has real words on it.
cards.tellNo: Look closer at the shop sign — the letters melt into made-up squiggles. Computers still can't spell on signs. A real photo has real words.

cards.cap: WORST morning of my LIFE 😱 (you won't BELIEVE what happened)
cards.question: Is the STORY real?
cards.tellOk: The photo's just a kid eating cereal. The drama is bolted on to make you click. Real life doesn't come with red arrows.
cards.tellNo: The picture's ordinary, but the story isn't. The shocked caption and red arrow pointing at nothing are bolted on to make you click. A true picture can carry a false story.

cards.question: Real, or a story bolted on?
cards.tellOk: No drama, no arrow, no ALL-CAPS panic. Just a normal post. When nothing's trying to yank your feelings, it's usually just... true.
cards.tellNo: This one's real and plain. Notice there's nothing trying to grab you — no shock face, no arrow. The absence of bait is itself a signal.

💰 Nobody gains if you share this

cards.cap: HAPPENING NOW — Bramblebrook high street UNDER WATER 🌊 share so everyone knows!!
cards.question: Looks real… but is it from TODAY?
cards.tellOk: The photo is real — the 'happening now' isn't. It's a nine-year-old flood picture dug up to look like today's news. The picture can't tell you that; only checking the source can. That's why you check.
cards.tellNo: Tricky — the photo is completely real. But it's nine years old, and 'HAPPENING NOW' was bolted on today. You can't see that in the pixels — only a source check shows it. An old truth, re-posted as new, is a lie.

lines: 📅 Photo first posted 9 years ago
📍 Taken in a different county
🔁 Re-posted every time it rains

cards.cap: 9 out of 10 kids CAN'T balance a coin like this 😲 are YOU in the 1%?
cards.question: Do the numbers add up?
cards.tellOk: Do the maths: if 9 out of 10 can't, then 1 in 10 can — that's 10%, not 1%. Nobody counted anything. The numbers are only there to make you try it, comment and share.
cards.tellNo: Check the maths: '9 out of 10 can't' means 10% can — so where did 'the 1%' come from? Nobody counted anything. Made-up numbers dressed as facts are a tactic: they sound precise, so you don't check.

lines: 🧾 No quiz or count linked anywhere
📊 A '9 out of 10' claim every single day
💬 Every post begs for comments

cards.cap: just woke up like this, total mess 🥱 #nofilter
cards.question: Candid, or staged?
cards.tellOk: 'Total mess' — with perfect light, perfect hair and a breakfast tray styled like a magazine? This took an hour to set up. The lie isn't the photo; it's the word 'candid'.
cards.tellNo: Look again at the 'mess': perfect light, perfect hair, a styled breakfast tray. Real just-woke-up doesn't look like a magazine. Staged photos pretending to be accidents are a tactic — the lie is the word 'candid'.

cards.cap: This school just BANNED break time 😡 SHARE if you think this is WRONG
cards.question: Is the ANGER real?
cards.tellOk: Anger is the product. No school is named, no rule is shown — just an empty playground and 'SHARE if you're angry'. Rage makes you share before you think, and shares are the payout.
cards.tellNo: Count the facts: no school named, no letter, no rule — just a photo of an empty playground and an instruction to be angry. The story is a feeling with nothing under it. Manufactured outrage is a tactic: anger spreads faster than checking.

lines: 🏫 No school is named anywhere
📰 Account is 3 weeks old — not a news site
💰 It earns money when posts go viral

cards.cap: Our park was PERFECT until the new lot from Grimley Road moved in 😤 everything's worse now
cards.question: Who's really being blamed?
cards.tellOk: Look at the evidence: some litter. Look at the claim: a whole group of people ruined everything. Nothing connects them. Blaming a group for everything is a tactic with a name — scapegoating — and it works because anger feels like evidence.
cards.tellNo: The evidence is a messy bin. The claim is that a whole group ruined everything — with no proof, just 'them'. That tactic is called scapegoating: pick a group, pin every problem on them, and let anger do the thinking.

lines: 🗑️ Same litter problem for years
👤 Only ever posts about 'the new lot'
🤝 Grimley Road is never asked

cards.cap: FREE game credit codes 🎮 DELETING IN 1 HOUR ⏰ share with 3 friends to unlock
cards.question: Why the countdown?
cards.tellOk: The clock is the trick. 'One hour' exists to stop you thinking, and 'share with 3 friends' is the real goal — you're the advert. There are no codes.
cards.tellNo: Real giveaways don't need a panic timer. The countdown exists so you don't stop to check, and 'share with 3 friends' is the point — the post spreads itself through you. The codes never existed.

lines: ⏰ The '1 hour' post is 6 days old
🎮 The game says codes aren't given this way
🔁 Thousands shared and got nothing

cards.cap: I gave a stranger £100,000 and changed his life forever ❤️
cards.question: Is the FEELING real?
cards.tellOk: Follow the money. The giving isn't the kindness — it's the footage. The stranger is a prop, the emotion is the product, and 8 million views is the real payout. Ask who profits from you feeling this.
cards.tellNo: Don't judge the man — judge the system. The giving isn't the kindness, it's the content. The person is a prop and the emotion is the product. The tell isn't in the picture; it's in who profits from you feeling this.

lines: 💰 Ads earn more than he gives away
🎬 A 12-person film crew in the credits
📈 The 'stranger' is in 3 other videos

cards.question: Real, or engineered?
cards.tellOk: Past tense, a real small number, a named place, and no ask to share. When nobody is farming your feelings, it's usually just true.
cards.tellNo: This one's real — £214, past tense, nothing begging to go viral. Compare it with the £100,000 giveaway: the difference isn't the kindness, it's who the camera is for.
